_pre_score_comment: Hard trend thresholds applied before GPT — stocks failing any are dropped without an AI call. null = no limit for that direction.
_limit_order_comment: Caps buy price at pre-flight quote + buffer% for both paper and live (e.g. 0.5 = 0.5% above). null = market orders (uncapped slippage). Set to 3.0 on 2026-08-06 after two straight days of scripts/analyze_scoring.py-visible slippage data showed market orders on fast-moving names paying far more than quoted: 2026-08-05 ZETA +10.4%, GTE +10.5%; 2026-08-06 ASPN +12.9%, HNST +19.4% (that one alone turned a would-be +20.5% winner into a +0.9% wash). 3.0 was chosen to block that >=10% tier while still letting most picks fill -- across those two days, 7 of 25 fills had slippage above 3% (18 of 25, i.e. 72%, would still have filled unchanged). Tradeoff: a capped LMT order can simply not fill on the fastest movers within fill_wait_seconds, so this trades some missed entries for capping catastrophic ones. Revisit by comparing fill-rate and slippage stats before/after in scripts/analyze_scoring.py once enough data accumulates under the new setting.
_bracket_comment: Stop-loss fires at -stop_loss_pct% below fill price. take_profit_pct locks in gains at +take_profit_pct%. Set either to null to disable.
_enhanced_data_comment: Each source can be independently disabled (e.g. if a scraper starts getting blocked) without a code change. max_tickers bounds worst-case wall-clock time since these are synchronous scrapers with no per-ticker concurrency.
_trailing_stop_by_risk_comment: When enabled, overrides the flat trailing_stop_pct above with a per-pick stop width keyed by GPT's risk (1-5): tighter for high-risk picks (cut losers faster) and wider for low-risk/high-conviction picks (let winners run), instead of stopping every position out at the same distance regardless of how risky it was flagged. Falls back to trailing_stop_pct for any risk value not listed. Only takes effect when trailing_stop_pct is set (same mutual-exclusivity rule as before).
_catalyst_type_weights_comment: Conviction/allocation multiplier applied per catalyst_type (1.0 = neutral). Derived from scripts/analyze_scoring.py's win-rate/return breakdown of 390 historical picks (keyword-classified pre-catalyst_type era): ma_acquisition was the worst performer (22.6% win rate, -30% total return contributed over 31 picks) so it is discounted; analyst_action was the best performer (54.1% win rate, +36.7% total return over 74 picks) despite catalyst_prompt.txt's WEAK CATALYST RULE treating it as a soft catalyst, so it is boosted. fda_approval and short_squeeze are the classic explosive-outlier catalysts and are kept neutral (1.0) rather than discounted -- fda_approval's historical -0.85x came from only 3 samples (too small to trust, and directly opposite the goal of catching big binary-event moves) and short_squeeze has 0 historical samples. Revisit all of these once enough native (post-catalyst_type-field) data accumulates -- run scripts/analyze_scoring.py periodically and adjust.
_risk_penalty_comment: Allocation penalty for risk>=threshold picks (applied as score * factor before score^2 weighting). Historically risk=3 picks had the HIGHEST total return of any risk bucket (95 picks, +47.5% total) -- possibly a small-sample artifact, but the penalty is kept configurable rather than hardcoded so it can be disabled/tuned as scripts/analyze_scoring.py accumulates more data without a code change. threshold raised 3 -> 5 on 2026-08-06: the 2026-08-05 SIZE RULE fix now tells GPT to set risk 4-5 on genuine Profile A outlier catches (not just weak/soft ones), so a threshold of 3 was double-penalizing exactly the picks that fix was built to surface -- risk 3-4 were getting both a tight trailing_stop_by_risk AND half allocation weight, while the trailing stop alone already carries that risk. Live data backed this up: 2026-08-05/06 combined, risk>=3 picks got only 8-15% of total capital despite including the best single performer both days (GTE +0.52%, ASPN would have been +10.3% without slippage). Threshold=5 keeps the discount only on the most extreme tier, which the risk rubric itself defines as 'genuine catalyst or not' at 50%+ moves -- the one tier where caution regardless of catalyst quality still makes sense.
